And it is possible to interpret this regarding the person himself— in that being a human, created in the image of God, he already possesses reliable ground to be a faithful emissary to his Sender, Who created him of the speaking species endowed with intellect.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And even though in his present intellect he cannot fathom how rectification is possible, he nonetheless has faith that the deep has split open for him—meaning the future blessings— when the Blessed Name will clarify all Jewish souls and restore them all, as it is written (II Samuel 14:14): “And He devises means so that the banished one not remain cast out.”

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Shabbat 104a: ‘The Gemara cites another midrash that also deals with the letters of the alphabet. This one uses a code in which the first letter is paired with the last letter, the second letter with the penultimate one, and so on [alef tav, beit shin]. Alef tav, God said: If he despised Me [oti ti’ev] would I desire [etaveh] him? Beit shin: If he does not desire to worship Me [bi], shall My name [shemi] rest upon him? Gimmel reish: He defiled his body [gufo]; shall I have mercy [araḥem] on him? The word comprised of the letters gimmel and reish in Aramaic means licentiousness. Dalet kuf: He locked My doors [daltotai], shall I not cut off his horns [karnav]? To this point, the Gemara interpreted the…’ Context and connection to Sichat Shedim: In Sichat Shedim 1, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Shabbat 104a) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this is the mystery of "falsehood has no legs" (Shabbat 104a), and the teaching that demons' feet resemble roosters' claws (Berakhot 6a; Gittin 68b); and here is not the place to expand. And this was effected...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the metaphysical nature of shedim, the rectification of fallen sparks and human imagination through Torah, and the absolute unity of Divine Providence developed in Sichat Shedim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Wherefore when our father Jacob perceived his immense holiness ("an adder in the path", Bereishis 49:17), he imagined that he would never die and was King Mashiach! However, those who are submerged in the lusts of this world of falsehood are likewise designated "lame"; for "falsehood has no feet," as stated in Shabbat (104a); and as known in the mystery of: "her feet go down to death" (Mishlei 5:5), where resides the primary dominion of the husks; the feet symbolizing the organs of lust: "he had neither dressed his feet" (II Shmuel 19:25), and "at her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay" (Shoftim 5:27).

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And this explains what is brought in the Talmud (Shabbat 119b): “Whoever recites Vayechulu becomes a partner with the Holy One in the work of Creation,” for the primary purpose of Creation was that creatures recognize His sovereignty and unity and crown Him over all, and without this heaven and earth could not endure; it turns out that the person who possesses this conscious recognition.

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Berakhot 6a: ‘One who seeks to know that the demons exist should place fine ashes around his bed, and in the morning the demons’ footprints appear like chickens’ footprints, in the ash. One who seeks to see them should take the afterbirth of a firstborn female black cat, born to a firstborn female black cat, burn it in the fire, grind it and place it in his eyes, and he will see them. He must then place the ashes in an iron tube sealed with an iron seal [gushpanka] lest the demons steal it from him, and then seal the opening so he will not be harmed. Rav Beivai bar Abaye performed this procedure, saw the demons, and was harmed. And because of the overpowering force of their love and cleaving, this breeds a diminishment of awe and reverent etiquette, until it looks like contempt for holy matters, Heaven forbid.

Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: The meaning of epirus is the core root of its vitality, as recorded in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 14): that common folk refer to the soul as epirus; meaning that their entire life-force is invested in that specific fixed trait, and were it withheld from them, it would be identical to extinguishing their existence.

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And that is: because the attribute of Abraham is Chesed, to expand and multiply goodness unto all, the antithesis of the men of Sodom who sought to withhold kindness from benefiting anyone, as brought concerning them in the Talmud (Sanhedrin 109a): that they declared: “Come, let us cause the law of wayfarers' feet to be forgotten from our land”.

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Shabbat 77b: ‘On the subject of sores, the Gemara cites a statement referring to one of the methods for healing a sore. Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in His world, He did not create anything for naught. He created a snail as a remedy for a sore; He created a fly to be crushed and spread as a remedy on a wasp sting; He created a mosquito as a remedy for a snake bite; and He created the snake itself as a remedy for a skin rash; and He created a gecko as a remedy for a scorpion bite. The Gemara explains: How does one implement the remedy? He brings two geckos, one black and one white, cooks them, and spreads the resulting ointment on the affected area.’ Context and connection to Sichat Shedim: In Sichat Shedim 1, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Shabbat 77b) to illuminate his exposition here (“As in Shabbat (77b): everything created serves a beneficial purpose; and in the Future all will be rectified, no creature perishing: "The wolf shall dwell with the lamb," "and dust shall be the serpent's meat"; and...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the metaphysical nature of shedim, the rectification of fallen sparks and human imagination through Torah, and the absolute unity of Divine Providence developed in Sichat Shedim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And into a 'transgression for Heaven's sake' as mentioned above in this world, so long as the evil inclination endures, from which the evil thought originates as noted; unless one attains such a transcendent spiritual level wherein it is revealed to him that the inclination itself is likewise from Hashem, blessed be He, which realization constitutes the total nullification of the inclination completely as I wrote concerning this elsewhere, wherein even sinful thoughts are inverted into good.

Because Korach took a talit made entirely of techelet,” or sky blue, referring to the blue thread required on the tsitsit, made from the blue dye of the Chillazon snail.

Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And as it is said: "And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid, etc." (Yeshayah 11:6). And regarding the nations of the world it is said: "For then will I turn to the peoples a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of Hashem, to serve Him with one consent" (Tzefanyah 3:9); as written in Avodah Zarah (3b): that all gentiles will become proselytes who are drawn along in the Future; yet they will not be equal to the Children of Israel, for "Hashem alone did lead him" (Devarim 32:12).

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: Now the serpent was more subtle than any beast of the field. From this it appears that in the wild beasts of the field is found more wisdom than in domestic animals, for a domestic beast agrees in its mindset to be subjugated and disciplined under the hand of man, with man providing sustenance for its soul, and does not care to sustain its needs directly from Hashem's hand; whereas in the wild beast is found greater wisdom, in that it does not wish to receive its bounty through flesh and blood, and consents to live with measured austerity, provided that its sustenance be directly from Hashem, blessed be He, so that it gazes at all times unto the Giver.

Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: The explanation, as known from the mystical secret of running and returning like lightning seen by the visionaries of the Divine Chariot, is that to the place they go, there they return; meaning that where light reaches its final vanishing point, there it turns back, the end becoming the beginning in a continuous cycle, so that the end of all levels binds directly to the origin and depth of the Beginning, being called the head of all levels; for the Beginning of all is Hashem, blessed be He.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: So generation after generation: the second generation inherits goodness through the awe learned from the first; and inheriting from the earlier generation, though retaining awe (“Surely you will fear Me, you will receive instruction”), it inherits a trace of the failure as well; yet the first suffered agonizingly, buying Torah with their blood (damin), while the heir suffers mildly, acquiring with money (ma'ot).

English_Source_Translation_And_Context: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 18: “In Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 18), it is taught: Whenever a person sits and studies and utters words of Torah below, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits opposite him and reads and studies together with him—fulfilling ‘The Lord is your shadow upon your right hand’ (Psalms 121:5).” Context and connection to Sichat Shedim: In Sichat Shedim 1, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 18) to illuminate his exposition here (“[as in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 18) on Judges 18:6: "Were it not written it could not be said," as I explained there]; and just as Hashem rules over man who accepts His kingdom, so Israel will govern the human...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the metaphysical nature of shedim, the rectification of fallen sparks and human imagination through Torah, and the absolute unity of Divine Providence developed in Sichat Shedim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And as the Maharsha wrote in Chiddushei Aggadot there, that visitation is for the immediate hour while remembrance is for generations; examine there. Meaning that it is known that in the brain exists the chamber of memory, wherein are engraved and inscribed all things held in memory by a person, and a casual matter that one forgets has its engraving erased from that chamber and ledger of memory, but when he resolves in his heart to remember it, behold it stands continuously remembered by him, remaining engraved in his thought.

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: These are the generations of Noah, etc., Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood, etc. The concept of the Ark is that Hashem, blessed be He, gave counsel and protection to Noah until the days of wrath passed, and likewise for anyone whose heart has not yet been purified, he can learn strategies how to conceal himself and protect himself from every evil that rages in the world; and so our Sages of blessed memory said (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 6): if a person sees afflictions coming upon him, let him run to the innermost chambers of Torah, and she gives him counsel how to be saved.

Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: For Abraham sifted and purified all evil desires until he merited the Covenant in his flesh, which is the sign of that complete refinement, possessing no lust for evil, all desires being consecrated to Hashem. And this is woven into nature from birth and womb; thus by virtue of this covenantal sanctity he is not permitted to enter at all, merely standing at the portal without stumbling into the lust itself, for "your people are all righteous," and even uncircumcised Israelites are called circumcised.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Deuteronomy, Shoftim 7
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “You shall be wholehearted (tamim) with the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 18:13): wholeness (temimut) means walking before the Blessed Name with an undivided heart, without calculating future outcomes through divination or anxious schemes, trusting that at every moment God illuminates the step that lies directly before a person.
